required_changes.issue: _unaffected_literal lets corrections through to literal words that other units read as shared words. This weakens the old 'guarded file' rule beyond its intended scope. It has two holes. (a) It does not exclude units with `text_corresp`. Such a unit counts as realized, so before this change it was guarded and a correction to it failed. Now it passes, but `_range_segments` resolves `canonical_whole` callers of that URN to this unit's own segments. (b) It checks only whether the corrected part is itself a pointer or has an overlay. It never checks whether another unit points at that part through canonical/canonical_end, transclude, repeat, reuse, repeat_cue, citations or a spine reference, including a range that starts or ends in this unit and passes over an unidentified middle part. In both cases an unbound sic/corr goes into the generated file that those callers transclude. Their output changes with no attestation and no touches()/source_witness check, which is exactly the shared-words guard you asked about.
required_changes.evidence: canonical_corrections.py:62-78 excludes only canonical_home, canonical_parts, canonical_whole and reuse on the unit, and canonical, transclude, repeat or an overlay on the part. realizations.py:275-278 makes a unit with `text_corresp` a whole-text host. realizations.py:280-286 matches any unit's segment identity, not only canonical homes. canonical_corrections.py:177-196 (the reuse, transclude, repeat and spine checks) runs only over `bound`, and unbound items never reach it. The new test covers the pointer and overlay cases but neither of these.
required_changes.remedy: In _unaffected_literal: (1) return False if unit.get('text_corresp'). (2) Build the set of every URN referenced anywhere in readings. Strip '@…', split compact ranges with opensiddur.exporter.urn.split_range, and collect both endpoints. Cover every unit's segment canonical, canonical_end, transclude, repeat and repeat_cue target/corresp; unit canonical_whole, reuse values and citations (walk them the way check_citations does); and the expanded_order/source_order references, recursing into nested 'order'. Return False if unit['urn'] or any segment_identity of any segment in unit['languages'][lang] is in that set. Checking the whole unit, not just the part, is the cheap fail-closed way to catch ranges that span unidentified parts. Add two regression tests: a text_corresp unit that a canonical_whole caller resolves, and a mixed file whose literal paragraph is another unit's `canonical` target. Both must raise 'explicit shared home'.

required_changes.issue: The new mode's safety argument is that 'existing printing guards reject selecting its marked wording outside its attested caller'. Nothing requires the corrected `wording` to be a guarded feature. guards() takes its feature from the j:option that holds the canonical_printings pb. _bind_printing_correction only requires that a printing binding exist for (host, lang, identity). A literal-context home can carry more than one overlay on one identity, one per fragment (overlay_fragment). A correction in an option other than the one holding the pb would bind. At bind time only units' `wording_selection` is checked. A spine or other generated j:declare that selects that wording would not be caught by validate_generated:788-791. For 857 this does not happen: in the generated kohanim_yehi_ratzon_words.xml, pb `printing_kohanim_yehi_ratzon_s350` and the tei:choice sit in the same `…/printing/appendix` option. The general mechanism still fails open, though.
required_changes.evidence: canonical_printings.py:198-214 sets `feature` to the pb's ancestor option. canonical_corrections.py:36-38 checks only caller ownership. realizations.py:788-791 checks only guard features.
required_changes.remedy: In apply_bound_corrections, after the corrections are applied and the canonical_printings pb markers exist, require each binding with item['wording'] to have that wording equal some g['feature'] from canonical_printings.guards(documents, readings) where g['caller'] is one of the binding's attester stems, g['host'] == binding['host'] and g['lang'] == binding['language']. Otherwise raise. If apply_bound_corrections can run before canonical_printings.apply, put the same check in validate_generated instead: pass the bound corrections in, or add every j:option[@corresp] ancestor of a tei:choice/tei:sic in a canonical home to the guarded set, with the attesting caller. Add a test with two overlays on one identity and the correction in the option without the pb. It must fail.

notes: Generated sic/corr for 857 is correct. In kohanim_yehi_ratzon_words.xml, `<tei:choice><tei:sic>ללִבּוֹשׁ</tei:sic><tei:corr>לִלְבּוֹשׁ</tei:corr></tei:choice>` appears only inside j:option `…/printing/appendix`, after pb n=24 / n349.jpg, which is s350 and matches the attestation. The `…/printing/main` option still reads `וּבֶֽגֶד לִלְבּוֹשׁ` with no choice. The corr matches the user's ruling and the earlier printing's correct spelling. The context `וּבֶֽגֶד ` + sic + ` לְיַעֲקֹב` occurs once in the file.

kohanim_appendix_yehi_ratzon.xml declares appendix=true and main=false and transcludes `…/prayer`. musaf_kohanim_yehi_ratzon.xml declares main=true and appendix=false. So the correction is selected only in the attested caller.

_bind_printing_correction is strict where it needs to be. It requires the exact option locator; one matching option; a non-default index (>0); the context once in that option; the context absent from every host fragment and every other option; and every unit whose wording_selection sets the wording to True to be an owner with a printing binding, contain the exact canonical part, and attest the context once. Attestations must equal the expected (unit, scan) set exactly, with no duplicates and no host. The tests exercise these cases.
Classic bindings are unchanged. The only shared-path changes are the `item.get('wording')` rejection for non-home files and the `unaffected_witnesses` union, which is empty for classic bindings.

The review_payloads filter is correct. A wording-bound correction enters corrected_sha256 only when the realization's own settings select that wording as True. The host context (selection() makes the default True and the appendix False) keeps resolved == corrected. The caller keeps resolved == literal (sic) != corrected. corrected_text still fails closed if the context is missing from the resolved text.

Allowing the original host (musaf_kohanim_yehi_ratzon) as source_witness for spine references is reasonable, because it prints the unaffected default. A reference with no witness still fails (tested). Caveat: bind_corrections does not check that a spine occurrence naming the unaffected host witness does not itself select the corrected wording. That depends on the generated-document guard, so on the second required change, and spines are not generated yet.

apply_bound_corrections keeps the earlier invariants for the new mode: the sic projection equals the pre-correction projection, and the corr projection equals corrected_text over the whole file. The whole-file projection includes both options, so the separate uniqueness check is what makes this safe. Header text containing the context would fail closed.

Unguarded files that are canonical targets but have no pointers of their own (not 'realized') already accept unbound corrections under the earlier policy. That gap is older than this change and outside this review, but the remedy in the first required change could also be applied there later.
The tests follow repo conventions: unittest style, synthetic fixtures from test_marmorstein_canonical_printings, and no real project data.

Optional extra tests (not required for correctness): a second caller that selects the default wording keeps resolved == corrected in its payload; a spine occurrence that selects the appendix wording with source_witness=host is rejected once spines are generated; a correction context crossing a j:conditional or pb boundary fails closed in apply_corrections; the review payload changes when the correction's wording or attestation changes.
